entry: The nvdisasm ELF-file parsing interface; vendor text also contains the spelling nvdisam.
mechanism: Vendor-described read of freed memory while parsing a malformed ELF file. Exact allocation/free/use path is not established by the retrieved sources.
expected_behavior: Objective freed-memory-read evidence attributable to this target parsing path; generic crash or nonzero exit is insufficient.
affected_release_text: CUDA Toolkit releases up to and including 12.6U1, Windows and Linux; this is a product-release range, not a standalone nvdisasm build-number range.
fix_release_text: CUDA Toolkit 12.6U2 (the 12.6.2 release-notes archive identifies Update 2).
unknowns: Exact root-cause function, freed object identity and lifetime are not disclosed in the retrieved vendor/CNA material.

entry: nvdisasm ELF REL-section parsing, as described by the public Talos technical report.
mechanism: Vendor: heap-based buffer overflow. Talos: inconsistent relocation allocation/write bounds in a confirmed nvdisasm 12.9.88 build. Those build-specific technical observations are not local measurements.
expected_behavior: Objective heap out-of-bounds-write evidence bound to the specified REL parser root cause, target build and input identity; sanitizer text or ordinary crash alone is insufficient.
affected_release_text: NVIDIA vendor/CNA: CUDA Toolkit releases before 13.0 on Windows and Linux. Talos primary report confirms standalone nvdisasm 12.9.88; its roundup article separately mentions 12.8.90. Do not substitute either component build for the product-release range.
fix_release_text: CUDA Toolkit 13.0. Talos records vendor patch disclosure on 2025-09-23; this does not establish a locally observed patch diff.
unknowns: The recorded WSL Toolkit 12.8 release matches the vendor's broad affected range, but exact local root-cause applicability and trigger prerequisites have not been independently confirmed.
Vendor coverage says Windows/Linux; WSL-specific vulnerable-path behavior has not been demonstrated in this phase.

Talos primary report lists nvdisasm 12.9.88; its roundup lists 12.8.90. Preserve each source's build scope; do not infer that these are mutually exclusive affected versions or select a unique tested build.
Vendor/CNA CVSS is 3.3 while Talos CVSS is 7.8. The original input's 7.8 is a public technical-source rating, not a replacement for the vendor rating; neither rating is an Oracle predicate.
The original input labels component build 12.9.88 as a Toolkit upper bound. That mixed version space is not a qualified machine-readable affected-release rule.
The exact remediation code and earliest introduced build are unknown; input patch hypotheses are not a reviewed code diff.
No local CVE experiment or affected/fixed differential was performed.

entry: cuobjdump parsing DWARF debug abbreviation information in CUDA fatbin/cubin input, described by Talos with the dump-ELF interface.
mechanism: Vendor: stack-based buffer overflow. Talos: insufficiently bounded DWARF abbreviation-table processing in a confirmed cuobjdump 12.8.55 build. Published analysis is not a local trace.
expected_behavior: Objective stack out-of-bounds-write evidence bound to the specified DWARF parser root cause, target build and input identity; a generic signal or successful tool exit does not prove this CVE.
affected_release_text: NVIDIA vendor/CNA: CUDA Toolkit releases before 13.0 on Windows and Linux. Talos confirmed standalone cuobjdump 12.8.55; broad release coverage does not prove a particular local root-cause observation.
fix_release_text: CUDA Toolkit 13.0. Talos records vendor patch disclosure on 2025-09-23; exact fix implementation is not established by the retrieved report.
unknowns: The recorded WSL Toolkit 12.8 release matches the vendor's broad affected range, but local cuobjdump 12.8.90 is not the Talos confirmed build 12.8.55 and no local root-cause observation was collected.
Vendor coverage says Windows/Linux; WSL-specific trigger prerequisites have not been independently confirmed.
Vendor/CNA CVSS is 3.3 while Talos CVSS is 7.8; preserve source attribution rather than silently replacing the vendor score.
Original input fixed_code_summary/fix_mechanism asserts exact patch behavior without a retrieved fixed-build code diff; that claim remains unknown.
The earliest introduced version is not established by the retrieved material.
